text: The React useEffect hook runs after every render by default. To optimize performance, pass a dependency array as the second argument: useEffect(() => { fetchData() }, [userId]). This ensures the effect only runs when userId changes. According to the React docs, omitting the dependency array causes the effect to run on every render, which can lead to infinite loops if you're updating state inside the effect.
